title: Microbatch Morphing: runtime-driven seqlen clustering + speculative kernel hints
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current continuous-batching approach groups requests primarily by arrival time and a coarse seqlen bucket. This causes excess token padding and suboptimal kernel choices when workloads have multi-modal sequence-length distributions (e.g., mix of short prompts + long context prefill). Padding increases GPU memory use, reduces effective throughput, and raises per-token cost.

Goal: Implement a runtime-driven microbatch morphing system that: (1) dynamically clusters in-flight requests by tight seqlen bands using lightweight approximate histograms, (2) performs speculative kernel-hinting so the scheduler can choose optimized kernels per cluster (e.g., fused-attn for short, tiled-kernel for long), and (3) schedules prefill vs decode segments to minimize KV cache thrashing while preserving low tail latency.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change model weights or quantization profiles. It does not implement full per-tenant model variant routing (separate ticket).

Motivation: Small reductions in average padding across large hosted pools translate to meaningful cost and p99 improvements. For Dedicated customers, tighter packing improves utilization and can defer capacity purchases. The speculative kernel hints avoid expensive runtime introspection during hot paths while enabling better kernel placement for heterogeneous hardware (A100 vs L4e).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end system that observes incoming request seqlen distribution and forms microbatch clusters within a 5ms decision window
Median padding tokens per batch reduced by >= 35% on mixed workload synthetic trace compared to baseline
P99 latency during steady-state load reduced by >= 10% for prefill-heavy workloads in our performance dashboard
No user-visible correctness regressions; generated outputs identical to baseline for deterministic tokens in unit tests
Feature gated and behind runtime flag; rollout can be toggled per-customer and default-off for Dedicated during initial rollout
implementation_notes:
Design: runtime agent collects low-overhead sketch (fixed-size ring histogram) of recent seqlen arrivals per worker. When the sketch shows multimodal peaks, the packer triggers a microbatch-morph operation: it rearranges pending requests into 2-5 narrow seqlen clusters, emitting cluster descriptors to the local scheduler. The scheduler consumes descriptors and assigns a kernel hint (enum: DEFAULT, FUSED_SHORT_ATTENTION, TILED_LONG_ATTENTION) based on cluster statistics and hardware profile.

Prefill/Decode scheduling: For requests with long prefill + short decode, the prefill segment is scheduled earlier and pinned to a worker for KV caching; short decodes are coalesced but scheduled with higher priority to maintain decode latency SLO. We introduce a soft prefill priority that reduces KV eviction during bursts.

Speculation: kernel hints are advisory only; the kernel selection layer can still fallback to compatible kernels. Hints are encoded in existing request metadata to avoid new wire formats.

Telemetry: new metrics: microbatch_cluster_count, avg_padding_tokens_saved, kernel_hint_accept_rate, speculative_fallback_rate. Expose per-tenant views in Console and add to canary dashboards.

Rollout: feature flagged. Start internal canary (redwood-internal) -> staged host accounts -> opt-in Dedicated tenants -> global enable.

Runtime safety: ensure decision window has strict CPU budget (<= 5ms) and no blocking syscalls; implemented lock-free ring buffers where possible.

Performance experiments: compare baseline continuous-batcher vs morphing-batcher across three synthetic traces (short-heavy, long-heavy, bimodal) and two hardware targets (A100, L4e).
tasks: Design low-overhead seqlen sketch and validate memory/cpu budget
Implement cluster detection and microbatch morphing in packer module
Add kernel_hint field to internal request header and update scheduler to consume it
Prefill-priority heuristic: implement soft pinning for long prefill segments
Add telemetry metrics and dashboard panels
Benchmarks: run A/B tests on synthetic traces and record p50/p95/p99, throughput, and GPU memory
QA: deterministic correctness tests + fuzz generation for edge cases (seqlen=1, very long context, concurrent cancellations)
Rollout automation: feature flag gating + per-customer toggle in Console
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: clustering CPU overhead increases worker latency. Mitigation: microbenchmarks and strict CPU budget; if budget exceeded, fall back to time-based packing
Risk: speculative kernel hints cause increased fallback rate on older drivers. Mitigation: track hint_accept_rate and auto-disable hints for hardware with high fallback
Risk: KV cache fragmentation from prefill pinning. Mitigation: implement TTL-based pinning and eviction pressure monitoring
Risk: correctness regressions for streamed responses. Mitigation: integrate with streaming integration tests and require parity on deterministic tokens
